concerns.text: SC-003 ('The model inference time is < 100ms per material on CPU') has no anchoring user story and no supporting FR. The Problem Statement mentions 'reduce inference time to milliseconds' as a goal, but no US or FR covers inference-time measurement. Either add an FR (e.g., FR-008: measure and report per-material CPU inference time) and anchor it to US2, or remove SC-003.

FR-006 (constitution title audit) cites '(See Constitution)' but no user story. Constitution Principle VI/terminology constraint motivates it, but per traceability discipline it should either be anchored to a story (e.g., extend US2 or add a US for scientific-integrity deliverables) or explicitly noted as a constitution-mandated requirement outside the user-story list.

FR-006 requires an audit verifying 'the project title does not contain forbidden First-Principles terminology', and Technical Constraints forbid the term. But the ratified constitution's title is 'Predicting the Elastic Moduli of 2D Materials from First-Principles Calculations' — the exact project title the audit would check. The spec's own requirement is guaranteed to fail against the constitution it must comply with (FR-030). This is the same root cause as the prior kickback (T060c). The spec must state how this is resolved: either the project title is renamed (and the constitution amended per its Versioning procedure), or FR-006's audit target must be redefined to the spec/paper title rather than the constitution title. As written, FR-006 contradicts the constitution.

Problem Statement says 'maintaining a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) within an acceptable range' — 'acceptable range' is never defined anywhere in the spec, while SC-002 defines success only as a ≥10% relative MAPE reduction vs baseline. Constitution Principle VI references a ≤15% MAPE claim. Three different framings of the accuracy target with no reconciliation; pick one measurable statement and use it consistently.

FR-006 requires an audit verifying 'the project title does not contain forbidden First-Principles terminology', but the ratified constitution title IS 'Predicting the Elastic Moduli of 2D Materials from First-Principles Calculations'. The acceptance condition is unsatisfiable as stated — the audit can never pass against the current title. The spec must state what the audit checks (e.g., the spec/paper title, or a renamed project title) so the pass/fail condition is reachable.

'identifies at least 3 structural descriptors with significant contribution' — 'significant' is undefined and unmeasurable. State the evaluation rule, e.g., descriptors ranked in the top-N by permutation importance whose removal causes a MAPE degradation ≥ X percentage points, or a named statistical threshold applied to the permutation/SHAP outputs.

'enforcing a hard memory limit of 7GB via tracemalloc' — tracemalloc only measures Python-heap allocations; it cannot enforce a hard process-wide limit. Rephrase to a verifiable procedure, e.g., 'record peak memory via tracemalloc and assert ≤ 7GB' (measurement, not enforcement), so the FR is checkable.

Under-reach: the idea's methodology explicitly requires data from Materials Project AND AFLOW, plus the verified TMD paper (arXiv:2505.05891) supplementary elastic constants. The spec restricts to 'a single canonical public source per run (no mixing sources)' and drops AFLOW and the TMD supplement entirely. If single-sourcing is a clarifier-driven hygiene decision, the spec should say so and justify the reduced data coverage; otherwise restore the multi-source acquisition or name which source was chosen and why the others were dropped.

Drift toward an easier target: the idea and Constitution Principle VI define success as ≤15% absolute MAPE on held-out unseen families. SC-002 replaces this with '≥10% relative MAPE reduction vs a composition-only baseline', which can be met by a model well above 15% MAPE. The absolute MAPE criterion (or an explicit, justified redefinition) must appear in the success criteria.

Under-reach (minor): the idea expects 3–5 descriptors explaining ≥70% of variance in elastic moduli. SC-005 requires only 'at least 3 structural descriptors with significant contribution' with no variance-explained or magnitude reference. State the measured quantity and reference (e.g., cumulative permutation/SHAP contribution) or explicitly defer the threshold.

Under-reach (minor): the idea's methodology includes 5-fold cross-validation for robustness and a MEGNet benchmark 'where available'. Neither appears in the spec (FR-004 covers only the linear-regression baseline). If these were consciously descoped, note it; otherwise add them.

The ElasticTensor entity lists components '(C11, C12, C13, C33, C44, C66)' — this is the independent-component set for a 3D hexagonal crystal, not a 2D material. For a 2D (monolayer) elastic tensor the in-plane independent constants are C11, C12, C22, C66 (plus out-of-plane C13/C23/C33 if the layered supercell is retained). Using the wrong component set means the '6 independent components' completeness filter (Constitution VI) and the continuum-mechanics derivation of Young's/shear/Poisson are ill-defined for the stated target. Define the 2D tensor convention (e.g., the standard 2D stiffness matrix) and which components the completeness filter requires.

MAPE is an inappropriate error metric for Poisson's ratio (and near-zero shear components): Poisson's ratio can be zero or negative, making percentage errors undefined or explosively large. The spec should restrict MAPE to strictly positive quantities (Young's, shear moduli) and specify a different metric (e.g., MAE) for Poisson's ratio, or justify the choice.

'identifies at least 3 structural descriptors with significant contribution' — 'significant' is undefined. Permutation importance and SHAP magnitude are ranking tools, not hypothesis tests; without a defined criterion (e.g., permutation-importance delta exceeding a stated threshold, or a permutation test against shuffled targets) SC-005 cannot fail in a meaningful statistical sense. Specify the decision rule for 'significant'.

responses.response: Added FR-008 requiring measurement and reporting of per-material CPU inference time, anchored to US2; SC-003 now references FR-008.
responses.what_changed: New FR-008; SC-003 text updated to cite FR-008 and US2.

responses.response: FR-006 is now explicitly labeled a constitution-mandated requirement (Principle VI) outside the user-story list, and anchored to US2 for traceability.
responses.what_changed: FR-006 text now cites '(Constitution Principle VI; anchored to US2)'.

responses.response: Added a Terminology Resolution subsection: the project title is renamed to remove 'First-Principles' (constitution to be amended per its Versioning procedure), and FR-006's audit target is redefined to the project/spec/paper title, making the audit satisfiable.
responses.what_changed: New 'Terminology Resolution' subsection under Technical Constraints; FR-006 and Deliverable 6 reworded.

responses.response: Problem Statement now states the single measurable accuracy target: MAPE ≤ 15% for Young's and shear moduli (MAE for Poisson's ratio), consistent with SC-002/SC-006 and Constitution Principle VI.
responses.what_changed: Problem Statement accuracy sentence rewritten with concrete bound.

responses.response: FR-006 audit target redefined to the renamed project title and all spec/paper/deliverable titles (not the pre-amendment constitution title), with a concrete pass/fail rule; FR-009 specifies the audit script must exit 1 and write the JSON report.
responses.what_changed: FR-006 reworded; new FR-009 for audit script behavior (exit code and JSON output).

responses.response: SC-005 now defines significance concretely: descriptors ranked in the top 5 by permutation importance whose removal degrades Young's/shear MAPE by ≥ 2 percentage points, with cumulative permutation/SHAP contribution ≥ 70%.
responses.what_changed: SC-005 rewritten with explicit decision rule and numbers.

responses.response: FR-003 rephrased to a verifiable measurement: record peak memory via tracemalloc (plus OS-level RSS) and assert ≤ 7GB, rather than claiming enforcement.
responses.what_changed: FR-003 wording changed from 'enforcing' to 'recording and asserting'.

responses.response: Added a Data Sourcing Decision note in Assumptions: single-sourcing from Materials Project is a deliberate hygiene decision (consistent schema, single DFT protocol); AFLOW and the arXiv:2505.05891 TMD supplement are explicitly descoped for v1 with rationale and named as future work.
responses.what_changed: New assumption bullet documenting the single-source decision and descoping.

responses.response: Restored the absolute accuracy target as SC-006: MAPE ≤ 15% on held-out unseen families for Young's and shear moduli (MAE for Poisson), per Constitution Principle VI; SC-002 retained as the comparative criterion.
responses.what_changed: New SC-006 with absolute MAPE bound; SC-002 unchanged.

responses.response: SC-005 now states the measured quantity and reference: cumulative permutation/SHAP contribution of top-ranked descriptors must account for ≥ 70% of total importance mass, matching the idea's 3–5 descriptor / ≥70% expectation.
responses.what_changed: SC-005 includes the ≥70% cumulative contribution target.

responses.response: Added FR-010 requiring 5-fold cross-validation for robustness reporting; the MEGNet benchmark is noted as conditional (executed only where a pre-trained MEGNet checkpoint is available on CPU within the 7GB limit), documented as a conscious descope otherwise.
responses.what_changed: New FR-010 and an assumption bullet for the conditional MEGNet benchmark.

responses.response: ElasticTensor entity now uses the 2D convention: all 6 components (C11, C12, C22, C66 in-plane; C13, C33 out-of-plane for the layered supercell) are recorded to satisfy Constitution Principle VI's 6-component completeness filter, while the 4 in-plane components are required for prediction-target eligibility (Young's, shear, Poisson derivation). The reconciliation with the constitution filter is stated explicitly.
responses.what_changed: ElasticTensor entity rewritten; explicit reconciliation note added.

responses.response: Metric convention added: MAPE is restricted to strictly positive quantities (Young's and shear moduli); Poisson's ratio is evaluated with MAE (target ≤ 0.05). Applied consistently in Problem Statement, SC-002, SC-005, SC-006.
responses.what_changed: Metric convention subsection added; SCs updated.

responses.response: SC-005/FR-005 now define the decision rule: permutation-importance removal causing ≥ 2 percentage-point MAPE degradation on Young's/shear, cross-checked by SHAP magnitude ranking agreement, plus a permutation test against shuffled targets (p < 0.05) for the top-ranked descriptors.
responses.what_changed: SC-005 and FR-005 include the concrete significance rule.
